property_summary: For any address k passed by the owner to setKeeper, the recorded keeper() must equal k; the buggy version violates this because initialize ignores the keeper parameter, so setKeeper from the buggy contract can be separated by observing that keeper() still equals address(0) until setKeeper is called, but the real break is that the reference records the exact k while the bug records it only after an explicit setKeeper — so the rule 'after a successful owner call setKeeper(k), keeper() == k' holds on both, and instead the distinguishing rule must read the initial keeper state independent of any setKeeper.
change_summary: Ignore the _keeper parameter during initialization and set the initial keeper to address(0).
